Frequently asked questions about BMW engine replacement, reliability, and ownership costs.

mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned N47D20C (the 320d engine) runs £3,200–£5,500 supply-only, while a reconditioned S63B44 (M5/M6/X5M/X6M) runs £9,000–£14,000. Fitted costs add 10–24 labour hours depending on the engine. Use our diagnostic calculator for a personalised figure.

mainEntity.name: Which BMW engine is the most reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B58B30 is the most dependable modern BMW engine in our dataset — just 540 enquiries in 2025, mostly due-diligence not failures. From the older era, the M57D30 turbodiesel has the same bulletproof reputation. Both share one thing: regular oil changes are non-negotiable.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common BMW engine failure?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N47 timing chain stretch is our #1 enquiry driver — 1,450 enquiries in 2025. Cold-start rattle from the rear of the engine is the early warning; ignored, chain slip means a full engine replacement at £3,200–£5,500 recon.

It depends entirely on the generation. The N47 era (E90/pre-2016 F30) has a reputation for timing chain issues — but a 2016+ F30 LCI with the B47 diesel is genuinely reliable. The G20 with the B58 is the safest 3 Series ever made.

mainEntity.name: Which BMW engine should I avoid?

acceptedAnswer.text: No engine outright — but a pre-2016 N47D20C without a documented timing-chain replacement is the one purchase we consistently advise against. The engine itself is solid; the rear-mounted tensioner design is the problem. The N63's hot-vee architecture is also a high-cost risk.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my BMW timing chain is worn?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cold-start rattle for 1–2 seconds is the classic early warning. On the N47 and N57, listen for a metallic rattle from the rear of the engine on startup. On the B58, coolant loss from the expansion tank is the early signal. Caught early, it's a repair; ignored, it's a £3,200–£5,500 engine.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing a BMW engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Depends entirely on the car's value. Against a £35,000 G20, a £5,000 B58 recon is just 14% of the car's value — safe. Against a £4,500 E90, a £4,000 N47 recon is 89% — walk away. Our 70% BMW threshold is the line.

mainEntity.name: How long do BMW engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: A well-maintained BMW diesel (M57, N57, B47, B57) can exceed 200,000 miles. The B58 petrol is also proving durable — with proper servicing, 150,000+ miles is realistic. The N47's chain is the limiting factor, not the engine itself.

mainEntity.name: Which BMW generation should I buy?

acceptedAnswer.text: 2016+ F30 LCI with the B47 diesel or B48 petrol. You get the facelift architecture, revised chain hardware, and electronics update — plus depreciation has already done most of its work. For petrol performance, a G20 M340i is the sweet spot.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my BMW engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Listed on the VIN plate and in the vehicle documentation; block stamping is visible from below on most N47/B47 units, and on the cylinder head on N52/B58 engines. Tell us your model year and variant and we'll identify it.
